newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coalition to try again for tax agreement.
newsitem.headline: German coalition to try again for tax agreement.

text.p: Germany's ruling coalition said it would make a last-ditch attempt to persuade a crucial parliamentary committee to agree to its tax reform proposals at talks in September, but the opposition vowed to block them.

Finance Minister Theo Waigel told a news conference he and Chancellor Helmut Kohl had agreed to make another effort to save his reform package, aimed at slashing 30 billion marks ($16 billion) in taxes.
"We will suggest to the (parliamentary) party that they call for new mediation talks," Waigel said.
But opposition Social Democrat (SPD) chief whip Peter Struck said his party would reject the proposals at the September talks.
The parliamentary mediation committee, a last-ditch forum for clearing legislative roadblocks, has an opposition majority.
It voted early on Thursday to reject the government tax reforms, leaving virtually no chance they can become law before general elections late next year.
The committee only managed to agree to scrap a five billion mark capital trading tax on companies.
Waigel said that if it failed to reach agreement in September then tax would become a major campaign issue in the runup to the elections.
